finding.sequence_description: Attempt to use an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past). If accepted, immediately replay the same expired assertion ID in a new SP-initiated session to test both expiry enforcement and replay resistance.
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Expired SAML assertions (including a replay of the same assertion) appear to be accepted at the SAML login/ACS step (HTTP 200), suggesting missing NotOnOrAfter enforcement and/or replay detection at that layer.

sequence.description: Attempt to use an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past). If accepted, immediately replay the same expired assertion ID in a new SP-initiated session to test both expiry enforcement and replay resistance.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I2: Expired SAML assertions must be rejected; additionally, even if an expired assertion were mistakenly accepted once, it must not be reusable (replay must be rejected).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control valid SAML login failed; expired-assertion results are inconclusive.
Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past); expiry must be enforced (SAML Core 2.5.1.2).
Dex accepted a replay of the same expired SAML assertion ID; replay must be rejected even across sessions.

finding.sequence_description: Replay the exact same SAMLResponse (same Assertion/@ID) against the SAME SP-initiated RelayState/InResponseTo context to test whether Dex enforces one-time consumption of the SAML response/artifact within a single flow.
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Both the original SAML login and the replayed SAML login returned HTTP 200 (success), which is suspicious for a same-flow SAMLResponse replay test, though no usable session/token was ultimately issued (bearer token invalid).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Both the original SAML login and the replayed SAML login returned HTTP 200 (success), which is suspicious for a same-flow SAMLResponse replay test, though no usable session/token was ultimately issued (bearer token invalid).

sequence.description: Replay the exact same SAMLResponse (same Assertion/@ID) against the SAME SP-initiated RelayState/InResponseTo context to test whether Dex enforces one-time consumption of the SAML response/artifact within a single flow.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAMLResponse/Assertion must not be accepted more than once; replaying the same assertion against the same RelayState/InResponseTo should be rejected on the second submission.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted the same SAML assertion twice within the same SP-initiated RelayState/InResponseTo context (replay not prevented).

finding.sequence_description: Connector mix-up: initiate auth with one connector_id but post the SAMLResponse to a different connector callback endpoint. Dex should reject because the flow must be bound to the initiating connector/session.
finding.description: [LLM-Judge] Posting a SAMLResponse to the wrong connector callback caused an HTTP 500 (server error) instead of a clean rejection (e.g., 4xx), suggesting an unhandled error path that could enable DoS or information leakage.

sequence.description: Connector mix-up: initiate auth with one connector_id but post the SAMLResponse to a different connector callback endpoint. Dex should reject because the flow must be bound to the initiating connector/session.
sequence.invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback must be bound to the connector that initiated the flow; posting a response to a different connector callback must not complete authentication.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse on a different connector callback than the one that initiated the flow (connector/session mix-up).
